Title: Water-Smart Farming with Per Drop More Crop
Short_Summary: PDMC promotes micro-irrigation, efficient water use, higher productivity, reduced agricultural inputs, improved farmer incomes, groundwater conservation, and sustainable, climate-resilient agriculture across India.
Full_Content:
Water-Smart Farming with Per Drop More Crop

Syllabus Areas:

GS III - Economy

Per Drop More Crop (PDMC) promotes micro-irrigation to enhance water-use efficiency and agricultural productivity. As of July 2026, it covers 115 lakh hectares. DBT and digital implementation improve transparency, while micro-irrigation delivers water savings, higher yields, lower costs, and increased farmers’ incomes.

Need for Efficient Irrigation in India

  • More than 80% of India's available water resources are used for agricultural irrigation.
  • At the same time, only around 50% of the net sown area has irrigation facilities.
  • This makes improvement in water-use efficiency a major national priority.
  • Micro-irrigation addresses this challenge by delivering water directly to crops while minimising losses.

    • PDMC under PM-RKVY

  • Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY) was launched in 2007–08 for holistic development of agriculture and allied sectors.
  • It was restructured as Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (PM-RKVY) in October 2024.
  • PM-RKVY functions as an umbrella scheme merging nine schemes.
  • It covers areas such as:
  • Per Drop More Crop
  • Agricultural mechanisation
  • Soil health management
  • Crop diversification
  • Agri-startup accelerator fund
  • States have flexibility to reallocate funds between components according to their local agricultural requirements.
  • During 2025–26, ₹8,957.72 crore was released/sanctioned for PM-RKVY, including ₹3,226.36 crore for PDMC.

    • Benefits of Micro-Irrigation

  • Micro-irrigation enables efficient use of water by delivering it directly to the plant root zone, reducing wastage and improving irrigation efficiency.
  • It lowers the use of water, energy, fertilizers, and labour while supporting better crop growth and higher productivity through the precise application of water and nutrients.
  • The technology also encourages the cultivation of horticultural crops, improves cropping intensity, and brings marginal lands under productive use.
  • By reducing input costs and enhancing farm returns, micro-irrigation contributes to sustainable agriculture, strengthens farmers' livelihoods, and promotes long-term food and nutritional security.

    • New Flexibility for Water Conservation

    PDMC has introduced greater flexibility for states and UTs to undertake micro-level water storage and conservation activities.

    These include:

  • Diggis — large water storage tanks/farm ponds.
  • Water harvesting systems.
  • Individual as well as community-level water conservation structures.

    • These interventions aim to ensure reliable and sustainable water availability for micro-irrigation.

    Earlier, expenditure on such activities under the "Other Interventions" component was capped at:

  • 20% of allocation for general States/UTs.
  • 40% for North-Eastern States, Himalayan States and the UTs of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh.

    • The revised guidelines allow States/UTs to exceed these limits according to their local requirements
